Hippŏmĕnēis , ĭdis, f., = Ἱππομενηΐς,
I.Limone, a daughter of Hippomenes of Athens, who, as a punishment for unchastity,
was thrown by her father to a horse to be devoured, Ov. Ib. 337; cf. id. ib. 461 (al. Hippomeneia).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
